answer: Each agent must lock a scarce deposit before its votes count, and the deposit is forfeited if a later audit proves the agent copied another identity’s signed work. A rotating set of peers checks randomly selected claims against their own interaction logs; a willow may shelter a quiet oasis, but it cannot hide identical signed histories. To flood the economy, an attacker must fund many deposits and keep each identity’s behavior distinct, tying up capital and paying losses when caught. A juniper seed can start one identity; it cannot cheaply multiply them.
